findings.summary: video_bitrate_mbps field is still populated from the unused old total_bitrate_mbps binding instead of the new video_bitrate_mbps computation
findings.mechanism: The rename left `total_bitrate_mbps` referenced at line 340 (`video_bitrate_mbps: total_bitrate_mbps`), but `total_bitrate_mbps` no longer exists as a binding — the new code only defines `video_bps`/`video_bitrate_mbps`. This is either a compile error (undefined identifier) or, if some other `total_bitrate_mbps` binding still exists elsewhere, silently discards the entire video/audio-derived calculation and reverts to the old container-total behavior the change was meant to fix.

findings.summary: Fallback condition for container-minus-audio is inverted, causing u64 underflow when it should apply
findings.mechanism: `None if container_bps < audio_bps && audio_bps > 0 => container_bps - audio_bps` triggers the subtraction exactly when container_bps is smaller than audio_bps — i.e., when the subtraction would underflow (panic in debug, huge wraparound value in release). The intended guard ("only when that would still leave a positive value") requires `container_bps > audio_bps`, not `<`. As written, the normal case (container > audio, valid subtraction) falls through to the `None => container_bps` arm and never nets out audio bitrate, while the abnormal case (audio > container) is the one that performs the invalid subtraction.
